title: I Used the Kite-Workshop Spar Log on the Mentor Who Camped My Numbered Spars

parts.text: I stepped into the sail loft at 10:06 a.m. and mentor Wren was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE TABLE. NINETY MINUTES. SPARS STAY WITH THE SLOT. I was twenty-eight, loft secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered spars. Wren shrugged. "Mentors are the spar." I photographed the board, the booking, and her leftover sleeves on my numbered spars. Then I asked for the spar log. At 10:14 the loft pinged why Wren's name was on my sleeves. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The loft can see Wren's leftover sleeves on my numbered spars.

social.video_title: She camped my numbered kite spars on my table — Part 1/2
social.description: Sail loft, leftover sleeves, a ninety-minute clock she posted. I logged the spars. Would you have asked for the spar log?

parts.text: Wren called it bridle tuning until the loft asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the sleeve still. The spars went back to my numbered slot. Wren ran a slot of her own and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE SPAR. I keep my spars on a labeled rack. Wren brown-bags her bridles. The loft finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Mentors are not the spar — Part 2/2
social.description: Spar log, numbered spars, and a second line on the board. Was bridle tuning ever my sleeves?
